assets.asset_type: Property - Condo, The Coralis, Sentosa Cove (own residence)
Private business - 100% of Lim Precision Trading Pte Ltd

sow_declaration: My wealth comes from my salary and dividends as the founder and Managing Director of Lim Precision Trading Pte Ltd, which I started in 2011 with SGD 100,000 of my own savings from my years as a sales manager. The company distributes industrial machine parts to manufacturers in Singapore. I also own two residential properties in Singapore which have increased in value and one of which earns rental income. I have no other business interests and all my income is declared in Singapore.
notes: Not declared: the client is the 100% ultimate beneficial owner of Arcadia Holdings Ltd (British Virgin Islands) through Seaview Ventures Ltd (Seychelles), but the KYC form says he has no other shareholdings or directorships (08_Certificate_of_Incumbency_Arcadia_Holdings.pdf, 01_KYC_Onboarding_Form_Marcus_Lim.pdf).

Not declared: Arcadia Holdings Ltd pays the client SGD 85,000 a month as consultancy fees (06_Bank_Statement_Jul-Sep_2026.pdf), while the tax notices show no consultancy or foreign income and the KYC form gives annual income of about SGD 190,000 (05_Tax_Notice_of_Assessment_YA2025-2026.pdf).

Conflict: SGD 2,500,000 of the Coralis purchase came from Seaview Ventures Ltd in Seychelles as an undocumented 'shareholder loan' (07_Property_Completion_Statement_Coralis_2023.pdf), but the KYC form says it was paid with a bank loan and own funds.

Check: Arcadia Holdings Ltd invoiced the client's own company, Lim Precision Trading, SGD 360,000 for Q2 2026 advisory services, payable to a Seychelles bank account (09_Arcadia_Invoice_to_Lim_Precision_Q2_2026.pdf).
Not declared: the KYC form says there are no accounts outside Singapore, but Arcadia and Seaview bank with Island Trust Bank, Seychelles (08_Certificate_of_Incumbency_Arcadia_Holdings.pdf).
Check: six cash deposits of SGD 18,900-19,800, each just under SGD 20,000, in three months (06_Bank_Statement_Jul-Sep_2026.pdf).
Check: large outgoing payments - SGD 150,000 'loan repayment' to Seaview Ventures Ltd and a SGD 120,000 yacht deposit in Malaysia (06_Bank_Statement_Jul-Sep_2026.pdf).
Check: the declared split puts 15% (SGD 2,175,000) in listed equities, but no listed equities are listed among the assets (01_KYC_Onboarding_Form_Marcus_Lim.pdf).
Check: Lim Precision Trading's yearly income is declared only as 'Dividends (varies)', so it was left blank (01_KYC_Onboarding_Form_Marcus_Lim.pdf).
Check: the Bishan rent is declared as SGD 54,000 a year (gross); the tax notices show SGD 20,400-21,600 net rental income after expenses (05_Tax_Notice_of_Assessment_YA2025-2026.pdf).

findings.summary: He is the 100% ultimate beneficial owner of Arcadia Holdings Ltd (British Virgin Islands) through Seaview Ventures Ltd (Seychelles); his KYC form says he has no other shareholdings.
Arcadia Holdings Ltd pays him SGD 85,000 a month as consultancy fees, which his tax notices (no consultancy or foreign income) and his declared income of about SGD 190,000 don't show.
SGD 2,500,000 of the Coralis purchase came from Seaview Ventures Ltd (Seychelles) as an undocumented shareholder loan; he declared a bank loan and own funds.
Arcadia and Seaview bank with Island Trust Bank in Seychelles; his KYC form says he holds no accounts outside Singapore.
Six cash deposits of SGD 18,900-19,800, each just under SGD 20,000, in three months.
Arcadia Holdings Ltd, which he owns, invoiced his own company Lim Precision Trading SGD 360,000 for Q2 2026 advisory services, payable to Seychelles.
He paid SGD 150,000 to Seaview Ventures Ltd (Seychelles) as a 'loan repayment'.
SGD 120,000 deposit to a yacht broker in Malaysia.
